documents.title: Why cities are rethinking the minimum parking rule
documents.text:
For half a century, municipal planners across the region have required developers to provide a fixed number of parking spaces for every apartment or shop they build. The rule was devised at a time when car ownership was rising steadily and street parking was regarded as a nuisance to be eliminated. Increasingly, however, economists argue that the requirement has produced precisely the congestion it was meant to prevent, by making driving the cheapest and most convenient option and by spreading destinations so far apart that walking becomes impractical.

The financial consequences are considerable. A study commissioned by the Calloway planning office estimated that each underground space adds between 30,000 and 50,000 dollars to the cost of a development, a burden that is ultimately passed on to residents, including those who own no vehicle. Tenants without cars are therefore, in effect, subsidizing their neighbors' parking.

Several cities have begun to abolish the minimums altogether, leaving developers to decide how much to build. Early results are mixed. In some districts, new housing has been delivered more cheaply; in others, residents complain that nearby streets have filled with vehicles. Councilor Mateo Ruiz, who voted for the reform, concedes that it was introduced without adequate provision for permits. "Abolishing the requirement was the easy part," he says. "Managing the street is where the real policy begins."

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the article?
choices: Developers are lobbying for larger underground car parks everywhere
Car ownership has fallen so sharply that parking has become redundant
A long-held planning rule is being challenged on cost grounds
A council has been criticized for rejecting a proposed housing project
questions.explanation: The article explains that economists argue the minimum parking rule has raised costs and encouraged driving, and that cities are starting to scrap it.

questions.prompt: What does the article imply about residents who do not own a car?
choices: They bear costs for facilities they do not use
They are the main beneficiaries of the reform of the rule
They have been offered cheaper rents by developers
They support the abolition of the minimum requirement
questions.explanation: The study says costs are 'passed on to residents, including those who own no vehicle', so carless tenants are 'subsidizing their neighbors' parking'.

questions.prompt: What does Mr. Ruiz admit about the reform?
choices: The changes have raised the price of new housing
The vote was taken without any discussion in council
Developers have declined to build any new spaces
Street management was not planned thoroughly enough
questions.explanation: He concedes it was introduced 'without adequate provision for permits' and says managing the street is where policy begins.

questions.prompt: The word "burden" in the second paragraph is closest in meaning to
choices: reward
load
delay
measure
questions.explanation: The extra construction cost is something developers and later residents must carry, so 'load' fits.

documents.title: Reassessment of the Lindqvist logistics contract
documents.text:
To: Executive Committee
From: Priyanka Deshmukh, Head of Procurement
Subject: Recommendation concerning the Lindqvist logistics contract

Dear colleagues,

The three-year contract with Lindqvist Freight expires on 31 December, and I should like to set out the case for not renewing it on its current terms. Over the past eighteen months, on-time delivery has averaged 91 percent against a contractual target of 96, and although penalty payments have offset part of the shortfall, they have not compensated for the damage to relationships with two of our largest customers. [A]

It would be unfair to attribute these results solely to Lindqvist. Our own order volumes have been far less predictable than forecast, which has made it difficult for any carrier to plan capacity. [B] Nevertheless, the pattern of recurring delays in the northern region suggests that the problem is structural rather than seasonal.

I therefore propose that we invite tenders from at least three carriers, while offering Lindqvist the opportunity to bid on revised terms, including a lower penalty threshold and quarterly performance reviews. [C] A change of provider carries risk, particularly during the peak period, so I would recommend that any transition be scheduled for the first quarter. [D] I would be grateful for the Committee's decision by 15 October, so that the tender documents can be issued before the end of the month.

Regards,
Priyanka Deshmukh

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the e-mail?
choices: To report a breach of contract by a major customer
To propose a change to a supplier agreement
To announce that a carrier has gone out of business
To request approval for a larger transport budget
questions.explanation: Ms. Deshmukh recommends not renewing the contract on current terms and inviting tenders.

questions.prompt: What does the e-mail suggest about the cause of the delays?
choices: The carrier alone is at fault for each late shipment
Customers have caused the delays by changing orders
Seasonal weather has affected all regions equally
Neither party can be held entirely responsible
questions.explanation: She says it would be 'unfair to attribute these results solely to Lindqvist' because the company's own volumes were unpredictable, yet the problem looks structural.

questions.prompt: What is Ms. Deshmukh's view on the timing of any change of provider?
choices: It should avoid the busiest part of the year
It should take place before the contract ends
It should wait until the penalty threshold is lowered
It should be decided after the tender documents are issued
questions.explanation: A change 'carries risk, particularly during the peak period', so she recommends the first quarter.

questions.prompt: In which position marked [A], [B], [C] or [D] does the following sentence best belong? "This is not a position that the company can afford to maintain for another contract term."
questions.explanation: The sentence sums up the damage to customer relationships described just before it and prepares the acknowledgement of other factors that follows; at the later slots it would interrupt the proposal or the discussion of timing.

documents.title: Meridian Biosciences: Postdoctoral fellowship in microbial ecology
documents.text:
The Meridian Institute invites applications for a two-year postdoctoral fellowship, renewable for a third year subject to review, to study how soil microbial communities respond to repeated drought. The fellow will join a team of eight led by Dr. Sunita Rao and will have access to long-term field plots, a sequencing facility and a modest travel budget of 4,000 euros per year.

Candidates should hold, or expect to obtain before the start date, a doctorate in ecology, microbiology or a related field, and should be able to demonstrate proficiency in the statistical analysis of large datasets. Experience with field sampling is advantageous but not essential. The successful applicant will be expected to publish in peer-reviewed journals and to contribute to the supervision of two doctoral students.

The annual salary is 52,000 euros before tax, with a relocation grant of 3,000 euros for candidates moving from abroad. Applications should include a curriculum vitae, a research statement of no more than 1,000 words and the names of two referees, and be submitted through the Institute's portal by 15 April. Interviews will be held remotely in the first half of May. The Institute is committed to equal opportunities and particularly welcomes applications from candidates returning to research after a career break.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the posting?
choices: To announce the results of a study on droughts
To request funding for a team of eight researchers
To recruit candidates for a temporary research job
To advertise a course in statistical analysis
questions.explanation: The page invites applications for a two-year postdoctoral fellowship.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the field experience requirement?
choices: It is demanded of every successful applicant
It replaces the need for a doctorate
It matters more than statistical knowledge
Candidates lacking it are not ruled out
questions.explanation: Experience with field sampling is 'advantageous but not essential', so lacking it does not rule candidates out.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT required in an application?
choices: A research statement of limited length
A letter from the Institute's director
The names of two academic referees
A curriculum vitae and a short biography
questions.explanation: The page lists a curriculum vitae, a research statement and two referees; it does not mention a letter from the head of the Institute.

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence suggest about the Institute?
choices: It rejects applicants who completed a doctorate abroad
It offers a longer contract to those with a career break
It hopes to attract applicants with interrupted careers
It prefers candidates who have worked in industry
questions.explanation: It 'particularly welcomes applications from candidates returning to research after a career break'.

documents.title: Fenmore Conservatory: Masterclass series
documents.text: The Fenmore Conservatory is delighted to announce a series of three masterclasses given by the cellist Ingrid Solheim, taking place on 6, 13 and 20 June. Each session will be devoted to a single work from the standard repertoire, and participants will have the opportunity to perform for Ms. Solheim and receive individual feedback. Places for performers are limited to six per session and are allocated after a short recorded audition. Listeners may attend without audition. Performers pay 120 dollars per session; listeners pay 25 dollars, or 60 dollars for the full series. Early applications received before 10 May will qualify for a ten percent reduction.

documents.title: Audition application
documents.text:
Dear Conservatory Office,

I am a final-year student at the Halvorsen Academy, and I wish to apply to perform in the masterclass on 13 June. I recorded my audition yesterday and enclose the link. Since I am unable to be present on 20 June owing to examinations, I would like to attend the first masterclass on 6 June as a listener. I shall also be bringing my accompanist, Daniel Osei, who would like to attend as a listener at the same session.

I should be grateful if you could confirm the total cost, including the early-application reduction, since I am submitting this on 8 May.

Yours faithfully,
Maya Lindgren

documents.title: Re: Audition application
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Lindgren,

Thank you for your application and for the recording, which the panel has now reviewed. We are pleased to offer you a place as a performer on 13 June. Please note that the work chosen for that session is the Dvořák concerto, and your recording features a different piece; we would therefore ask you to prepare the first movement of the Dvořák.

As you applied before 10 May, the ten percent reduction applies to everything you book, including your accompanist's place as a listener. A listener's place for a single session is available at the standard rate. Payment is due within ten days of this message.

Kind regards,
Helena Brandt, Conservatory Office

questions.prompt: What does the reply reveal about Ms. Lindgren's audition?
choices: She sent in a different piece from the one required
She failed to meet the standard needed for a place
She applied after the date for early applications
She was asked to play for the full series of sessions
questions.explanation: Ms. Brandt notes that the session's work is the Dvořák concerto while 'your recording features a different piece'.

questions.prompt: How much will Ms. Lindgren pay for her place as a performer on 13 June?
choices: 108 dollars
25 dollars
120 dollars
132 dollars
questions.explanation: The performer fee is 120 dollars; with the ten percent early reduction it is 108 dollars.

questions.prompt: How much will Mr. Osei pay for the single session as a listener?
choices: 25 dollars
54 dollars
22.50 dollars
60 dollars
questions.explanation: A single-session listener pays 25 dollars, reduced by ten percent to 22.50.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about Ms. Lindgren's attendance at the series?
choices: She will take part in all three as a performer
She will miss the last of the three sessions
She will attend only the session on 13 June
She will miss the first of the three sessions
questions.explanation: She cannot attend on 20 June because of examinations, will listen on 6 June and perform on 13 June.

questions.prompt: What can be concluded from all three documents about the masterclass of 13 June?
choices: It is the only session open to listeners
It will be taught by the Conservatory Office
It will take place after the early application date
It centers on a work she must now prepare for
questions.explanation: The advertisement says each session is devoted to one work, the reply names the Dvořák for that session and asks her to prepare the first movement, and she performs on 13 June.
